title: F-16 Fighting Falcon - Recognition Features
content: The F-16 Fighting Falcon is a single-engine multirole combat aircraft. In remote sensing imagery, it can be identified by its distinctive cropped delta wing with leading-edge extensions, a single engine with a ventral intake, and a relatively small fuselage. Wingspan: 9.45m, Length: 15.06m. In high-resolution optical imagery (< 0.5m GSD), the F-16 appears as a compact, delta-winged aircraft with a characteristic bubble canopy. SAR cross-section: medium RCS due to engine intake cavity.

title: C-130 Hercules - Recognition Features
content: The C-130 Hercules is a four-turboprop military transport aircraft. Key recognition features in remote sensing: high-wing configuration with four propellers, distinctive T-tail with high horizontal stabilizer, fuselage with upswept rear loading ramp. Wingspan: 40.41m, Length: 29.79m. The large wingspan and high-wing design make C-130s easily identifiable in medium-resolution imagery (1-3m GSD). SAR signature: large, high RCS due to corner reflectors formed by wing-fuselage junction.

title: B-52 Stratofortress - Recognition Features
content: The B-52 Stratofortress is a long-range, strategic heavy bomber. Recognition features: swept wings with 8 engines in 4 underwing pods, distinctive large fuselage, bicycle landing gear configuration. Wingspan: 56.4m, Length: 49.05m. The B-52 is one of the largest aircraft identifiable in remote sensing imagery due to its massive wingspan. SAR signature: very high RCS, especially from the engine pods and fuselage.

title: UH-60 Black Hawk - Helicopter Recognition
content: The UH-60 Black Hawk is a utility helicopter. Remote sensing recognition: four-bladed main rotor (visible as blur in low-shutter imagery), T-tail configuration, turbine engines mounted above fuselage. Length: 19.76m, Rotor diameter: 16.36m. Helicopters are typically identified by their distinctive rotor disk or parking configuration at helipads. In SAR imagery, the rotor blades create a distinctive Doppler signature when rotating.
